title: Rashmika Mandanna Suffers Hip Tendon Injury on Set, Advised Six Weeks Rest
excerpt: The pan-India star reportedly sustained a complete tendon detachment during a dance sequence, forcing schedule adjustments across four film projects and nearly 30 brand commitments.
body:
• Rashmika Mandanna has reportedly suffered a complete hip tendon detachment during a demanding dance and action sequence
  • Doctors have advised six weeks of complete rest followed by a structured rehabilitation programme
  • The injury is expected to affect shooting schedules for Ranabaali and Mysaa, plus nearly 30 brand endorsement commitments
  • This is the second major injury for the actress in 18 months, following a foot fracture in January 2025

Rashmika Mandanna has reportedly suffered a serious hip injury while filming an intense dance sequence for one of her upcoming projects, according to multiple industry reports on Thursday. The actress, who is currently working on Ranabaali and Mysaa, sustained what medical professionals have described as a complete tendon detachment in her hip.

Doctors who examined her noted that this type of tendon injury is more commonly seen in athletes undergoing rigorous physical training. She has been advised to take complete rest for the next six weeks to allow the injury to heal, followed by a structured rehabilitation programme focused on regaining strength and mobility.

A Packed Schedule Under Strain

Mandanna has been managing one of the busiest schedules in Indian cinema, balancing the shoots of four major films while also fulfilling endorsement commitments for nearly 30 national and international brands. The injury is expected to force adjustments across her ongoing film schedules and advertising assignments.

The actress recently completed an underwater action sequence for Mysaa — billed by its makers as India's first female-led underwater fight scene — before moving on to the Ranabaali schedule with Vijay Deverakonda. She had posted an appreciation note for the Ranabaali team just weeks ago, calling their work "something extremely scary."

Second Major Injury in 18 Months

This is the second significant injury Mandanna has dealt with in a relatively short span. In January 2025, she sustained multiple fractures and a muscle tear in her foot during a gym workout, leading doctors to prescribe three months of bed rest. She returned to work within 30 days, later revealing that she filmed a high-energy song for Thamma while still in considerable pain.

"I was in so much pain, I can't even begin to tell you," she said in an interview at the time, adding that the shape of her foot had permanently changed from the strain. Despite the injury, she attended promotional events for Chhaava in a wheelchair, flew between Hyderabad and Mumbai, and continued working on Thama, Sikandar, and Kubera.

""I was in so much pain, I can't even begin to tell you," she said in an interview at the time, adding that the shape of her foot had permanently changed from the strain."

Industry Response

While there has been no official statement from the actress or her team regarding the latest injury, fans have taken to social media to send wishes for her speedy recovery. Production teams associated with her upcoming projects are expected to revise their schedules during the recovery period.

The injury raises broader questions about the physical demands placed on leading actors — particularly those juggling multiple high-intensity projects with tight deadlines. Mandanna's previous decision to return early from her foot injury, against medical advice, underscores the industry pressures that often override recovery timelines.

Box Office Track Record

Mandanna has established herself as one of Indian cinema's most bankable stars. She holds the distinction of being the only actress with three Rs 500-crore blockbusters — Animal, Pushpa 2: The Rule, and Thamma. Her upcoming slate, including Ranabaali and a reported reunion with Allu Arjun for Raaka, will depend on the pace of her recovery over the coming weeks.
